principle: A guard break can preserve threat-facing authority by converting linear recoil into a support-owned pivot; the exit plant arrests rotation before the guard fully reopens.

noodle_queen.contempt: It does not read as mannequin symmetry, equalized spacing, planted-feet theater, straight tweening, reverse interpolation, floating guard, or an idle reset.
noodle_queen.function: Support ownership, root travel, guard authority, first plant, rotational overshoot, counter-travel, restack, and late guard recovery remain causally legible.
noodle_queen.taste: The compression-to-pivot phrase has a specific hooked silhouette and threat-facing guard attitude rather than a generic backstep.

tango_iteration_1.correction: Lift the old rear foot in D013-K08..K10 until D013-K11 reacquisition, and exaggerate D013-K06..K07 head/guard lag plus free-leg sweep so rear-anchor rotation is visibly distinct from a lateral slide.
tango_iteration_1.highest_value_visible_defect: During the first single-exit-foot support phase, the old rear foot still sat on the floor in the rendered ASCII, contradicting declared support ownership and making the pivot read as planted-feet theater.

tango_iteration_2.judgment: Final 33-frame render reads as asymmetrical brace -> guard crush -> rear-anchor pivot -> visible cross-body sweep -> honest single-foot exit plant -> rotational overshoot -> counter-rotation -> second-foot reacquisition -> late guard reopen -> secondary settle -> displaced ready debt. The corrected old rear foot is visibly clear of the floor during EXIT_FOOT ownership, and contact is not farthest reach.
